title: Test Drive
build: Decibel and Eagle Soft Incorporated side A, Eagle Soft Incorporated side B

records.c: Relocated entry word $B56B followed by body length $0A95 for GS.
Increment $63 twice before inspecting the two-byte counter at $53–$54. The interlude is invoked by the road-completion path at $6DD1.
Right-shift elapsed time $53-$54 and the accumulated speed $55-$57 together until the high time byte is zero.
Repeatedly subtract the remaining byte of elapsed time from the speed subtotal. The quotient in X is written to $BFCC. A zero time bypasses the repeated subtraction.
Add 60 per unit in $69 to the low time byte $68, subtract the per-stage constant from $BFE8 and clamp negative results to zero.
Fetch the stage's word from $BFF2 and derive a points subtotal. The repeated subtraction increments the award by four. The result is written to $BFCD-$BFCE and added to $43-$44.
Choose the final stage display when $52 is 4. Other stages prepare two picture IDs, run DP and GP, and set the interlude IRQ.

Drain pending keyboard input and clear the fire latch. Copy the character ROM range $D800-$DBFF to $E400-$E7FF with I/O switched out, then use CIA timer bytes and the tick counter to select an interlude message.
Read one zero-terminated message line. Skip high-bit bytes, stage remaining glyphs at $BFA4 and fill out the 40-cell line with spaces.
Convert the 16-bit value in A and X to five decimal digits by repeated subtraction. Put the digits in the results text, optionally replacing initial zeroes with $80.
Enable I/O and acknowledge the VIC interrupt, disable sprites, count a tick, then service a pending buffer swap, input and music before returning to the KERNAL IRQ.
Toggle the VIC bank bit when the main program requests a swap. Exchange the bitmap base, matrix base and bank-dependent scratch fields before clearing one pending swap.
Select the next raster phase using $BCE4-$BCE8, then combine the display-mode bits with its per-phase value.
Read the packed bitmap width, height and position, skip the six-byte header and calculate the destination in the active bitmap bank.
Use the resident $0824 service with Y set to $F2.
Invoke UJ using the supplied two-byte picture identifier and free that identifier's original packed item afterward.

The first three bytes precede the result text. Subsequent bytes encode message lines with indices $01-$1A for the alphabet and $20 for spaces. A zero ends a line and $FF separates message groups. The initial group has slots filled with the speed, time and points.
Forty glyph slots copied and filled with spaces by $B912.
Byte quotient produced by the average-speed loop at $B580.
Points award saved here before adding it to the running total.
Chosen message offset from $BFD0, selected by the timer and tick mix at $B82A.
Eight choices from $00, $03 and $06. The interrupt setup stores the selected value in $BFCF.
Workspace for five decimal glyphs. The conversion starts its digit writes at $BA1C.
Low bytes of 10,000, 1,000, 100, 10 and 1. Used by the digit conversion at $BA0A.
Companion high bytes for the repeated-subtraction digit routine.
Five words indexed by twice $52. The time calculation subtracts the selected word at $B5D7.
Five words selected by stage and divided by the adjusted time to form the interlude's points.
